newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Indian copper demand to hit 600,000T by 2005.
newsitem.headline: Indian copper demand to hit 600,000T by 2005.

text.p: India's copper consumption is seen expanding sharply to around 420,000 tonnes by 1999/2000 and over 600,000 tonnes by 2004/2005, the deputy secretary of the Ministry of Mines of India said on Tuesday.
Sanjeev Ranjan said at a copper conference here economic liberalisation has "resulted in a significant growth in industrial activity which in turn has spurred the demand for copper."

But copper metal production capacity has reached only 47,500 tonnes a year and the huge gap between output and demand has fuelled the construction of more smelting refineries using imported copper concentrates. The refining capacity of India is expected to reach 560,000 tonnes by 2002.

"Artificial constraints on copper consumption have been progressively removed while the easier investment climate and reduction in import duties has promoted a number of new smelter/ refinery projects," he said.

Of the total projected copper demand of 420,000 tonnes in 1999/2000, some 300,000 tonnes will be in the form of refined copper. In the case of the 600,000 tonnes needed for 2004/2005, about 450,000 tonnes will be refined copper and 150,000 tonnes will be scrap.
Ranjan said India has an estimated reserve of eight million tonnes of copper, but developing the resources is prohibitive because many are low-grade copper deposits.
